The MINERvA experiment uses a fine-grained hydrocarbon scintillator-based tracker.
The average antineutrino energy used in this experiment is 6 GeV.
Neutrons interact with the MINERvA detector by scattering inelastically, producing recoil protons or de-excitation photons.

The GENIE modification drops 35% of neutron candidates with energy deposit less than 10 MeV.
